The '''2024–25 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team''' represented [[Colorado State University]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Rams were led by seventh-year head coach [[Niko Medved]] and played their home games for the 59th season at [[Moby Arena]] in [[Fort Collins, Colorado]]. They participated as members of the [[Mountain West Conference]] for the 26th season. They finished the season 26–10, 16–4 in Mountain West play to finish in second place. They defeated Nevada, Utah State, and Boise State to win the Mountain West tournament championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the NCAA tournament as the No. 12 seed in the West region. They defeated Memphis before losing to Maryland in the second round.

On March 25, 2025, head coach Niko Medved left the team to take the head coaching position at [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-25 |title=Niko Medved leaves Colorado State for his native Minnesota after an NCAA tournament run by the Rams |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mens-college-basketball/news/niko-medved-leaves-colorado-state-for-his-native-minnesota-after-ncaa-tournament-run-by-rams |access-date=2025-04-03 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> On March 26, the school named assistant [[Ali Farokhmanesh]] the team's new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-27 |title=Colorado State promotes Farokhmanesh to HC |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44422934/colorado-state-tabs-top-assistant-ali-farokhmanesh-head-coach |access-date=2025-04-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Previous season ==
The [[2023–24 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Rams]] finished the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] 25–11, 10–8 in [[2023–24 Mountain West Conference men's basketball season|Mountain West play]] to finish in a tie for sixth place. They defeated [[2023–24 San Jose State Spartans men's basketball team|San Jose State]] in the first round of the [[2024 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West Tournament]] and [[2023–24 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Nevada]] in the quarterfinals before losing to [[2023–24 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|New Mexico]] in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 10 seed in the Midwest Region where they defeated [[2023–24 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the First Four before losing to [[2023–24 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] in the first round.
